title: Auth
summary: Authentication, session, identity-provider, and user-profile endpoints.
auth: Mixed surface. Provider discovery and login bootstrap paths may be public, while profile and user-scoped config endpoints require an authenticated session or API key.
purpose: These endpoints establish identity, inspect the current user, and manage the per-user LLM analysis configuration.
overview_points: Use provider discovery and login routes to start browser authentication flows.
Use `/v1/me` endpoints to read the current user and manage user-scoped LLM analysis settings.

title: Runs
summary: Run ingestion, run state changes, run browsing, comparison, and review endpoints.
auth: Protected. Expect a valid API key or authenticated session with access to the target run or project.
purpose: This is the core operational surface for creating runs, streaming events, approving or rejecting outcomes, and inspecting detailed run data.
overview_points: Use `/api/runs` and `/api/compare` for richer platform UI and review data access.

title: Projects
summary: Project creation, listing, membership, and API key management endpoints.
auth: Protected. Project membership or admin access is required for most operations.
purpose: Projects scope access, ownership, and API keys for shared evaluation work.
overview_points: Use project endpoints to provision new shared workspaces.
Use the API key sub-resources to create project-scoped credentials.

title: Analysis
summary: AI-powered analysis, previews, summaries, and related configuration endpoints.
auth: Protected. Analysis endpoints generally require access to the run and a valid user or project analysis configuration.
purpose: Use this surface when you want clustered failure analysis, preview runs, or analysis configuration tied to a stored run.
overview_points: Analysis endpoints usually operate on an existing run ID.
The platform UI surfaces these features, but the API is useful for automation and batch workflows.

title: Admin
summary: User administration, project administration, and health/operability endpoints.
auth: Mostly protected and admin-only, except for health probes which are usually public inside the deployment boundary.
purpose: Use these endpoints to bootstrap the platform, manage users, or integrate health checks into deployment automation.
overview_points: Use `GET /healthz` for liveness and smoke checks.
Use admin endpoints only from trusted operational contexts.

title: Ingestion
summary: SDK and pipeline ingestion endpoints for uploads, event streaming, and submission flows.
auth: Protected. These endpoints are intended for SDK and automation clients authenticated with API keys or trusted sessions.
purpose: These endpoints accept new run artifacts and event streams from SDK or pipeline producers.
overview_points: Use upload and event endpoints when you are pushing results into the platform from SDK or CI flows.
The same run lifecycle can later be reviewed through the richer runs surface.
